summary: Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and Harvard University (~1951–1957), where he later served as a professor from ~1969 to 1996.

Masayuki Taira (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held posts at Kansai University (~1983–1992), Osaka University (~1992–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2016).
Masumi Mochizuki (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Minobusan University, where he is attested as a Buddhist Studies faculty lecturer in 2001 and as a professor in 2015.

Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth, and has served as a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal since 1992.

Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar. Attested in 2012, he earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang.
Matthew Immergut is a religious studies scholar who studied under Culadasa. In 2011, he is attested as Associate Professor of Sociology at the State University of New York at Purchase.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Thupten Champa, and doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, completing his PhD at the University of Toronto by 2014.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, the University of Hawaii (MA), and Duke University (PhD attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Brown University and UC Berkeley, and held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002–2018).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber (1857–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1864–1868), the University of Würzburg (~1868–1874), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1874–1892).

Matthieu Ricard (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, earned a PhD at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob (~1967–1972), and studied under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1979–1991).

Mattia Salvini works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski (~2004–2009) and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (~2011).

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at South Carolina, Furman, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and Johns Hopkins under Charles Rockwell Lanman, becoming a professor at Johns Hopkins in 1881.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from ~1955 to 1979.
Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar. He was educated at Tonbridge School (~1937–1942) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1945–1950).

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure. She studied at the University of Manitoba (~1939–1943) and under traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani (~1966–1973) and Eido Tai Shimano (~1971–1977).

Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was an archaeology, history, and Indology scholar. He served as a professor at Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (attested 1994) and Editorial Committee Director at Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente (~1995–2000).

Mauro Maggi is an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at University of Naples "L'Orientale." He held posts at University of Hamburg (1990), Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, and Sapienza University (attested 2018).
